.NET Rules

.NET Rules

Comprehensive .NET development rules covering C#, ASP.NET Core, Blazor, Avalonia, CI/CD, testing, and solution architecture

Introduction

Section titled “Introduction”

The .NET rules provide comprehensive guidance for modern .NET development across all platforms and application types, from web APIs to desktop applications, with emphasis on performance, maintainability, and industry best practices.

Note

Rule Interdependencies: Many rules reference and build upon other rules to ensure consistent code generation.

For example, ASP.NET Core rules automatically incorporate C# coding style guidelines, so all generated API code follows the same performance patterns, memory management, and modern language features.

This creates a cohesive development experience where all code maintains consistent quality and style across different technologies.

Available Rules

Section titled “Available Rules”

General .NET Development

Section titled “General .NET Development”
Solution Structure Rules Proper .NET solution organization with Directory.Build.props, global.json SDK pinning, and build configuration
Testing Rules Comprehensive testing strategies using xUnit with unit and integration testing patterns, mocking, and test data management
Benchmarking Rules Performance testing and benchmarking using BenchmarkDotNet with micro-benchmarking and profiling integration
Library Development Rules Best practices for creating and maintaining .NET libraries, NuGet packages, API design, and semantic versioning
Dependency Management Rules Safe management of NuGet dependencies with security considerations, license compliance, and vulnerability scanning

C# Coding Style Rules Modern C# coding standards with latest language features, performance patterns, and maintainable code practices

Fast Endpoints Rules High-performance API development using the Fast Endpoints library for scalable web services

General .NET Development

Section titled “General .NET Development”

Solution Structure Rules

Section titled “Solution Structure Rules”

The Solution Structure Rules provide guidance for organizing .NET solutions with consistent build configuration, SDK management, and project structure. These rules ensure maintainable, scalable solution architectures across teams and projects.

What It Does

Section titled “What It Does”

This rule enforces proper .NET solution organization by:

  • Standardizing solution-wide build properties through Directory.Build.props
  • Managing SDK versions consistently with global.json
  • Establishing consistent project structure and naming conventions
  • Configuring EditorConfig for code style enforcement across the solution

File Patterns

Section titled “File Patterns”
  • *.sln and *.slnx solution files
  • Directory.Build.props and Directory.Build.targets
  • global.json and nuget.config
  • Project organization in logical folder structures

Testing Rules

Section titled “Testing Rules”

The Testing Rules establish comprehensive testing strategies using xUnit framework with patterns for unit testing, integration testing, test data management, and continuous testing practices.

What It Does

Section titled “What It Does”

This rule provides guidance for:

  • Implementing effective unit and integration testing strategies
  • Using xUnit framework with parallel execution and test categories
  • Establishing mocking strategies and test data management
  • Configuring test environments and CI/CD integration

File Patterns

Section titled “File Patterns”
  • *.Test.*.csproj test project files
  • tests/**/*.cs test source files
  • Test configuration and setup files

Benchmarking Rules

Section titled “Benchmarking Rules”

The Benchmarking Rules provide guidance for performance testing and benchmarking using BenchmarkDotNet, enabling developers to measure and optimize application performance systematically.

What It Does

Section titled “What It Does”

This rule establishes:

  • BenchmarkDotNet integration for micro-benchmarking
  • Performance testing methodologies and best practices
  • Profiling integration and metrics collection
  • Continuous performance monitoring in CI/CD

File Patterns

Section titled “File Patterns”
  • *.Benchmark.csproj benchmark project files
  • benchmarks/**/*.cs benchmark source files
  • Performance test configuration files

Library Development Rules

Section titled “Library Development Rules”

The Library Development Rules provide comprehensive guidance for creating, maintaining, and publishing high-quality .NET libraries and NuGet packages with proper API design and versioning.

What It Does

Section titled “What It Does”

This rule covers:

  • NuGet package creation with proper metadata and versioning
  • API design principles and backward compatibility
  • XML documentation and API surface analysis
  • Semantic versioning and release management

File Patterns

Section titled “File Patterns”
  • libs/**/*.csproj library project files
  • Package configuration and metadata files
  • API documentation and specification files

Dependency Management Rules

Section titled “Dependency Management Rules”

The Dependency Management Rules ensure safe and secure management of NuGet package dependencies with focus on security, licensing compliance, and vulnerability management.

What It Does

Section titled “What It Does”

This rule provides:

  • Package security scanning and vulnerability detection
  • License compliance checking and management
  • Automated dependency updates with security patches
  • Dependency conflict resolution strategies

File Patterns

Section titled “File Patterns”
  • *.csproj project files with PackageReference
  • packages.lock.json dependency lock files
  • nuget.config package source configuration

C# Coding Style

Section titled “C# Coding Style”

C# Coding Style Rules

Section titled “C# Coding Style Rules”

The C# Coding Style Rules establish modern C# coding standards leveraging the latest language features, performance patterns, and maintainable code practices for building robust applications.

What It Does

Section titled “What It Does”

This rule enforces:

  • Modern C# language features (C# 13) including collection expressions and primary constructors
  • Performance-oriented patterns with Span<T>, Memory<T>, and ValueTask
  • Memory management best practices with ArrayPool and stackalloc
  • Code quality standards with analyzers and nullable reference types

File Patterns

Section titled “File Patterns”
  • All *.cs files in .NET projects
  • *.csproj project configuration files
  • .editorconfig and analyzer configuration files

  • Proper error handling and API documentation

File Patterns

Section titled “File Patterns”
  • Program.cs for application configuration
  • appsettings.json for environment configuration
  • API controller and endpoint files
